Conclusions 9 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 Research Findings in Capital Costs, Operating Costs, and Suitability Microsimulation The findings of this research task are presented in the development of an economics model of fleet operation. The first modeling tool is designed to assess the capital and operational costs and benefits of fleet electrification at a fleet-level scope. For this research, we refer to microsimulation as a type of simulation in which entities, in this case vehicles, are modeled at the individual level but have less decision autonomy than in an ABM. The purpose of our microsimulation model is to estimate the suitability and cost of eMDHD vehicles for any fleet setting, i.e., any composition of vehicles performing any variety of duty cycles, operating from (and, potentially, charging at) the same home location.
